policy: One rules file for the logger and the Kismet plugin. The logger is the only classifier; the plugin shows the logger's results.
class=device: a MAC block assigned to a vendor whose radio products are law-enforcement equipment. A hit is written to law_enforcement.sqlite with match_reason 'Hardware: ...'.
class=fleet: a vendor that also sells the same kind of equipment to civilian, commercial, transit, utility, fire/EMS or enterprise buyers. A hit alone goes to Review, never to the LE log.
class=name / laa / agency: text a device broadcasts (SSID, device name) or a locally administered prefix. Anyone can set or collide with these. Review only.

Kismet's manufacturer text is looked up from the MAC's OUI, so it is never independent confirmation of the OUI. 'manuf' strings below are only a fallback for blocks Kismet knows but this file does not list, and count as the same evidence as the OUI.

Learned: a device with a direct association observed by Kismet (dot11 client_map / last_bssid / associated_client_map) to a confirmed LE device (Hardware or Operator) is written as 'Learned: ...'. Learned rows are never parents, so nothing cascades past one hop.
A probe for an SSID does not identify an access point. Probes only ever produce Review notes.
Signal strength is never used as evidence.
Operator marks are stored in archimet_review.sqlite (overrides + audit) and written to the LE log as 'Operator: ...' with the note, time and source.

learning.note: A confirmed AP with more than max_clients_per_parent learned clients stops teaching; further clients go to Review as possibly shared. An AP joined by confirmed hardware is learned only if its SSID is not public and Kismet lists at most shared_ap_client_threshold associated clients for it.

Not found in the IEEE registry extract of 2026-10-20; removed rather than guessed.
Process automation / IT, not ELSAG ALPR.

excluded.what: Manufacturer needles with no match in Kismet's manuf table
excluded.why: taser international, utility associates, mobile-vision, kustom signals, wolfcom, reveal media, edesix, visual labs, getac video, coban technologies, elsag, perceptics, vigilant solutions, rekor, soundthinking, brinc, federal signal, whelen, soundoff signal, code 3, applied concepts, efjohnson, bk technologies, l3harris, novatel wireless, digi international, panasonic system communications, vitronic, autel robotics, grayshift. Kismet derives manufacturer text from its OUI table, so these strings can never appear.

gaps: Digi International: no entry under that name in the IEEE extract; Kismet's table lists 00:40:9D as 'DigiBoard'. Not mapped. Digi routers are matched by model name only (Review).
Vendors with no IEEE block (Wolfcom, Reveal, Edesix, BRINC, Whelen, SoundOff, Code 3, Vigilant, Rekor, Getac Video, COBAN Technologies) cannot be detected by MAC on this system.

Bluetooth: the Pi's linuxbluetooth source reports no service UUIDs (0 of 622 devices, 2026-10-21) and no advertised names, so BLE UUID and BT-name rules are inert. Axon BT is detected by its public 00:25:DF address only.
Randomized (locally administered) MACs defeat OUI matching. They can only be logged through a learned association or an operator mark.
Kismet's REST API does not expose 802.11 vendor IE bytes, so vendor-IE signatures are not possible here.
In-car laptops on generic Intel/Qualcomm Wi-Fi are not identifiable by MAC; they can only be learned by associating to a confirmed in-car AP.
